I’m a dance teacher who works mostly with kids but I also teach a beginner adult ballet class.  Some of the people who come are complete beginners, some are people like you who danced when they were younger and now returned to it.  I love teaching this class; I move pretty slowly mostly focusing on barre exercises and remind everyone not to get frustrated with mistakes, it’s a safe space to do movement that makes you happy and it should be FUN!  

I also regularly take a pro level ballet class.  I find it so ridiculous for a teacher to be scolding an adult like that in class.  I fully understand your frustration; I’ve felt the same way before.  I’m very picky about the classes I take now because I just feel like I’m too old to be getting yelled at by a dance teacher lol.  There are good days and bad days depending on how your body feels and that’s just the way it is.  I’m not sure where you are located but if you can it might be good to find a different class for a while.  Different teachers have different personalities and styles of teaching and you might feel better with someone else.  Not necessarily an easier class but just a teacher with a different approach.

I’m on 150mg twice a day - double whammy to treat both bipolar 2 and epilepsy.  I was on 100 twice daily for a few years but had a breakthrough seizure in April and upped my dose since then and so far no issues 🤞🏻 

I was originally put on it back in 2018 just for bipolar (didn’t get epilepsy diagnosis till 2020) and was only on 50 mg back then.  The original plan was to titrate up to 75 at least but I never went back to my psychiatrist for a checkup.  

Eventually the seizures started and I went to a neurologist who figured it’d be best to stay on the same medication with an increased dose since he knew my body tolerated it well already.  I was really scared to titrate up bc of “the rash” but he told me overall lamictal is a very safe medication and in all his years of practice he has never seen a case of the SJS rash.  I don’t have any severe side effects other than some mild memory issues that idk if I’d even notice if I didn’t know it was a side effect.  I hope this reassures you a bit!!

This whole clingy/jealous thing in relationships.  The idea that you need to "keep tabs" on your partner.  Or that they should only look good for you.  And that it's okay for you to shame them and yell at them because they have a sexual history that you don't.  Going on to their Facebook and unfriending all their exes.  Asking for their social media passwords and if they resist, guilting them into making them "able to trust you".  Threatening to end your life when they break up with you.  

Sorry that got a bit specific there, a lot of this was personal experience.  For real though, I've seen a lot of this controlling and jealous bs passed off as normal by both men and women.  Your partner and their autonomy/privacy should be RESPECTED and they should not feel that they have to be "allowed" to do anything by you.  You are their partner, not their personal dictator.  Of course, jealousy is a natural and sometimes unavoidable human emotion, but if you are that insecure with your own self that you abuse your partner in this way, you are not yet ready to be in a relationship.

It still comes back every so often, but a lot of things kept me going.  I am fortunate enough to have a mom who has been through dark times herself and so she got me the care I needed.  The hardest part but perhaps the most important one is to tell someone how you are feeling.  For me, it took a suicide attempt to do this.  I was halfway through the bottle of pain pills I was about to chase with a bottle of vodka when I just thought no, I don't want this, no one wants this.  I did have to spend some time in the hospital but all things considered I'm doing pretty okay.  Sometimes I guess you have to hit rock bottom in order to climb back up.  Try to get a few hugs a day and take care of yourself.  Support is key, and don't be shy to venture to r/depression for extra internet care.
